task: Yes, in fact I think we do have a mission for you, <Ranger>. You see the nephew of our Parliament speaker, Rolan is a daredevil and an adventure-seeker. Always roaming the Galaxy greedy for gain. This time around too, the devil got him into this godforsaken miner place on the planet of <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system. And sure thing once again our hero has plu... sorry, I mean got himself into new trouble. We can't really say exactly what happened (this is something you should ask Rolan's wife about), but if you manage to solve the guy's problems by, say, <Date>, we will pay you a fee of <Money> cr. And, yes, we will give you directions to Rolan's wife. So what do you say? We have a deal?
success: The speaker is totally in awe of your actions! His gratitude is endless. Or rather it does have and end and that is <Money> cr. And please accept our congratulations as well - such zest in the resolution of our problems and the problems of our planet is nothing but inspiring.
loc.1.0:
At the main airport of <ToPlanet> you were given the directions to Rolan's place. As it turned out he was living on a remote island where spaceships almost never went. The dwellers of the island lived an isolated life according to some laws of their own. However the "islanders" made no trouble for the planet government, so the government lets them be.

Several hours later you finally made it to the island. Landing proved to be a trifle to difficult, than the flight itself. Struggling your way through turbulent streams you started to descend. Phew... Landed! No wonder no-one ever comes here. Contemplating the local weather conditions, you opened the hydraulic door of your ship. 

The sight outside was pitiful - a shabby cabin with a satellite antenna on top (apparently this is their means of communication with the outside world) and a landing platform, made of time-eaten asphalt. Looks like this place used to be an airport back a long time ago. While you were eyeing the empty surroundings, you did not notice a woman clad in work-clothes approach you. 

- Hello. My name is Ramina. Have you been sent by the <FromPlanet> government? - she asked.

- Yes. I was asked to settle the problem with Rolan. Oh by the way, <Ranger>'s the name, but you can call me "the greatest saviour in the galaxy of all times". Just kidding. Ha-ha.

- This is not the time to joke, - the woman responded. - Rolan has encountered some sort of a problem with the Iroquois gang, and they kidnapped him. The only time I heard from them they sent me a message, saying that if I did not pay them <clr>900 platinum pieces<clrEnd> (that's the local currency), they would kill him. Now I only have <clr>20 platinum pieces<clrEnd>, - the woman handed a small bag of coins to you. - Times is running out. <clr>only ten days left.<clrEnd> I don't know what to do... Maybe I should go to the Iroquois and try to convince them to return my husband? Although I do not think they would talk to you without money. In any event, you can use this truck, - the woman gave you the keys, - without one it is impossible to go anywhere in these parts. You will find <clr>the location map<clrEnd> in the glove compartment. Oh, and one other thing - sleeping in your truck (or let alone on the street) is very dangerous here because of the poisonous parasites. All right - enough of talking. While we are chatting here, my husband is sitting in some damp basement! - Ramina said tears in her eyes, and headed back to the cabin.
loc.2.0:
The insides of the cabin matched its outside - all of the furniture was ancient and looked like it was about t collapse. You looked at Ramina.

- Want to tell me something? Or else ask me something? - the woman said, holding two fluffy beasts on the leash. These looked like hairy crocodiles or something.
loc.2.1: - After the collapse of the bridge that led to the rubidium mines, things here got pretty tight. Then Rolan has got another of his crazy ideas, and he borrowed 450 platinum pieces from the Iroquois. But things did not go as planned and we did not manage to return the money on time. And the Iroquois don't like to be kept waiting. So they found out that Rolan had a rich uncle and kidnapped my husband, thinking that his uncle will pay them what is due plus the interest. But where would his uncle find platinum pieces pray tell? - with this words Ramina's eyes filled with tears.
loc.2.2: - Normally they would find everyone themselves... But if you are asking about their base, it is located <clr>in the east, right behind the Spinach farm<clrEnd>. Go straight east.
loc.2.3: - Dangers? This entire place is one big danger! The Scorpions and the Iroquois, collecting tolls control the roads. Plus there are all kinds of hoodlums here and there. Here you always have to keep your ears pricked. And one more thing, do not sleep in your truck or in the street - asides from the bandits there are all kinds of poisonous creeps here. The only place where you could feel more or less safe, I think, is <clr>Shpick<clrEnd>.
loc.2.4: - No, unfortunately not. At night my boys, - the woman nodded at the fluffy creatures at her feet, - tend to become aggressive - especially to strangers. They could eat you, you know. And I really do not feel like subjecting you to yet another danger. Too much depends on you... Oh, by the way! You can sleep for free at the <clr>miners' barracks<clrEnd>. Go to the <clr>Blue Rocks<clrEnd>, then turn <clr>south, to the miners' village<clrEnd>.
loc.2.5: - My husband used to be in trading. But I do not know whether you will be able to trade when you do not have the money... Although, somebody told me you could earn some extra from the miners by working in the coalmines. This way you will be able to make at least some sort of initial capital. Besides my husband told me that in <clr>Shpick<clrEnd>, that's the biggest town here, there is a demand for coal and scrap metal. You could buy coal from the miners as well.
loc.2.6: - The climate is rather dry. Days are clear most of the time, and at nights it gets darker, but it never gets completely dark. Which is why many people here would sleep when they are tired, not at nights.

loc.12.0: - So what do you want to know, gringo?
loc.12.1: - What weapons are you talking about, man! My brothers and me have found a couple of pieces at the dump site, but those are ours. I mean, in these parts, one needs weapons for himself.
loc.12.2:
- Thing is, back a long-long time ago there used to be a huge Maloq base here. It had been built even before the Interstellar Coalition was founded... 
The outpost stayed here for many years, but then it turned out, that most of the equipment has long been outdated. When the Maloq government learned about this, they ordered to dismantle all of the materiel, and extract those parts that were good for something at least, and abandon the base altogether. So the outpost command did just that. The military, dismantled all of the materiel, packed everything that was not outdated in large containers, and left, leaving this huge dump site behind. 
So, many-many years later my brothers and I - smart as we are - we found ourselves this cosy place. Now we are running a small family business and no Iroquois and Scorpions would ever tell us what to do! 

The guy raised the steel robot hand and you saw a sizeable blaster in it.
loc.12.3: - Rolan, eh? I think he owes the Iroquois money and they keep him hostage. Asking for a ransom... But that all I know, I'm afraid, - Cromalione said.
loc.12.4: - I am sure they will gladly buy it from you in Shpick. If you want to find it, go south to the miners' village and then turn to the east.

The Peleng took the coin from your hand, pushed a lever on some weird-looking unit, and thirty seconds later the unit belched out a portion of green mesh. Throwing THIS onto the plate, the Peleng stuck an iron spoon in it and handed it over to you. 

- Don't forget to return the dishes, - he growled.

You nodded in response.

The thing tasted even worse than it looked. You did swallow a couple of spoons, but with each new spoon you were felling sicker and sicker. Finally your stomach rebelled and you vomited. Apparently you were not <clr>that hungry<clrEnd>, to eat this green substance.

loc.23.2: - In Shpick - a town in the east, - the man answered.
loc.23.3: - Oh yeah?! You've come to the right place then. Our mines are always in need of fresh manpower. While working here, you can earn as much as three platinum pieces an hour. Not bad, eh?

- Hey you! What are you waiting for! Get this pickaxe and start working!!! - he boomed looking directly at you.

loc.46.0: - Looking for something? - the sheriff asked, his hand next to his gun-holster.
loc.46.1: - The Iroquois? You really think I will start messing with them because of some Rolan? I don't even know who he is. In any case, the Iroquois are always dead serious about what they say. If you want to talk to them, look for them in the east - right behind the Digsons' farm.
loc.46.2:
- Is that so? - said the sheriff and burst out laughing. - Listen here, lad, I bet you are not local in this parts. The Scorpions and the Iroquois have been collecting road tolls here over the past god-knows-how-many decades. And if I start a war against them now, chances are they will put an untimely end to my career, rather than I will to theirs...
The only way I can help you is with this advice. If you want to live, stop whenever these hoodlums demand you to and pay the toll. Or, if you are so tough, you can try and fight your way through. And one other thing <clr>if you are carrying cargo, the toll will be larger<clrEnd>. Because both the Scorpions and the Iroquois think that cargo transportation should be paid for extra. And the more the cargo, the bigger the pay. 
Or, maybe you have been talking about my lads here? Well, they never attack anyone, they only fine those who break the traffic rules. I mean, we need money for road repairs here, what did you expect? Then again, if you have doubts about the work of my lads, welcome to the penalty-lot and we'll take it from there...
loc.46.3: - Why did you say you understood in chemistry in the first place then?! Alright. Let's get out of here, - the sheriff told you.
loc.47.0: - You think I am as stupid as to give a to give a shotgun to a hoodlum like yourself? Just how arrogant you exactly are?! Then again... If you helped us, I might as well give you a pack of cartridges for a shotgun. You understand anything about chemistry?

- Excellent! - the sheriff exclaimed and waved you to follow him.

You went past the cells and some shabby-looking rooms, trying not to lose sight of the sheriff. Finally he took you into a small room where a thin lad was sitting and reading a book on some metal box. 

- Here. Got you a helper here. Says he knows chemistry. Explain what you got here...
- Errrrr. I am not going to make any drugs! - you hurried to make a point.
- Can you really? - the chemist looked surprise. 
You shook your head.
- Sorry to hear that. Anyway, we need your help for something different. We wanted to open this safe using cyclocalolic acid. It's almost ready - all I need to do is add g-luconate. The big question here is how much exactly is there in one gram? Hell knows. So I am trying to figure out - <clr> how many grams of Helios do I add instead of three grams of Vinon<clrEnd>?
- Any more information about it? - you asked.
- Well, yes, I did find something in this textbook.

The mixture of <clr>2 grams of Arben and 1 gram of Basol<clrEnd> contains <clr>the same amount<clrEnd> of g-luconate, as <clr>3 grams of Helios<clrEnd>.
<clr>2 grams of Basol<clrEnd> contain <clr>the same amount<clrEnd> of g-luconate as <clr>3 grams of Vinon<clrEnd>.
The mixture of <clr> 1-gram of Basol and 1 gram of Helios<clrEnd> contains <clr>the same amount<clrEnd> of g-luconate, as, <clr>1 gram of Arben<clrEnd>.

- Is that it? - you asked.
- Yep. So how many grams of Helios do we add? Any ideas? And yes, one more thing - the mixture with g-luconate is going to be very unstable. So if we add a wrong amount, it is going to explode for sure...

loc.153.0:
One of the villains walked over to your truck, swung the door open and pulled you out on the ground. He searched your pockets and called out to his comrade:
- This guy has got [p6] on him.
- The titanium-searcher says there's nothing in the truck either, - the second responded. - Looks like he's telling the truth. He is broke. Well. So what do we do with him?
- Look in the truck, maybe we could use some of his cargo - anything that looks valuable - load it in our SUV.
- He's got nothing in here either. He's empty...
- Shocks! Let's take the truck then. Sell it to Lou for spares.
This phrase was the last thing you remembered before a shot of pain knocked you unconscious. Looks like they knocked you out.

When you came to you were lying on the road. No truck, no money, nothing... Sitting by the side of the road you contemplated your future. But you could not think of anything. To kill the growing boredom you started catching the little flies that shot by. Big mistake. One of them bit you, your hand swelled enormously, and you died right there and then...
loc.154.0:
- No money, you say? Well let us have a closer look... - with these words the two villains started searching you, but only found [p6].
- Check this out, this geezer really does not have the money we need. 
- Does he not know that when one is going across the land of the Iroquois, one should be carrying a big fat bag of platinum pieces? Looks like this guy needs a lesson.

With these words the pair started battering you. Already after the fourth kick you lost consciousness.
loc.155.0:
The entire house was packed with all kinds of equipment. On the right there was a row of some medical (or so they looked) devices of all shapes and kinds. There was even some rusty unit that read "Dental Drill". Must be some ancient torture machine.

Right across from the door you saw a shabby sofa and a small guy clad in a white coat snoring on it. On his chest lay a round mirror with a hole and a band. As it appeared the medicine adept was not in the mood to work today but the way things are it also looks you will have to wake him. Knocking on the door loudly you woke the doctor.

- Eh? What? The only place in the Galaxy! Revolutionary methods of energy treatment. <clr>Complete treatment of wounds.<clrEnd> <clr>50 platinum pieces<clrEnd> only.
loc.155.1:
- Energy treatment, eh? No problemo, - the doctor took the money from you. Quickly he had you seated in the tough chair of the unit, put a helmet on your head, attached electrodes to your arms, fastened your wrists (completely ignoring your feeble protests) and, giggling in the most evil way, pulled the lever on the wall.

You felt an electric jolt shoot through your body. "That's it, I'm history!" - you thought. But no. The charge was slowly fading out, and you felt your body fill with energy. You closed your eyes and fell asleep.

When you woke up you felt an annoying pain.

- Wake up, dear- the doctor burred, slapping your cheeks. Seeing that you came to he started disconnecting the electrodes form you.

As soon as you were up, to your greatest surprise you understood you were indeed feeling much better. And although you were not feeling that lively, this was a minor.

- Anything else? - the doctor asked.
loc.155.2:
- In addition to that we perform operation on brain transplantation, remove hair from heels and fins (for Maloqs and Pelengs respectively), and, - the doctor came closer to you and whispered, - we also transplant sexual organs to the Faeyans. So what did you have in mind?

- No, thanks, none of the above for sure, - you answered quickly.

- Too bad. Too bad indeed. Anything else?

- I weighed your sack. Approximately <clr>a ton<clrEnd>. Good. <clr>Take your two platinum pieces.<clrEnd> Alright, gonna work more?
jump.81.desc:
You worked for all you were worth, but you were running out of strength. Suddenly your feet swam, and you sank down onto the ground.

- Is this one dead? - you heard a voice. - Let's see what's in his pockets.
You opened your eyes and saw two Pelengs looming over you. As soon as they noticed you were about to get up they took to their heels.
Apparently the workers got you out of the mines. And good riddance. Struggling back to your feet, you saw that you still did feel a bit better than before. Even lying on the bare ground does have a certain refreshing effect!
jump.83.desc: Hurray! You managed to get up. Moreover you did not even break anything. Looks like you got away with it fairly unharmed...
jump.86.text: Hit the SUV with your truck-side
jump.86.desc: You hit the SUV good! Sparks all around!
jump.87.text: Hit the SUV with your truck-side
jump.87.desc: With your eyes flaming you snapped the steering wheel to the side, skidding the truck onto the chasers. The spikes on your wheels caught the SUV damaging it badly. Now that the villains understood they were making a mistake they started manoeuvring, trying to move away from the danger zone.
jump.88.text: Shoot at the car from the shotgun
jump.88.desc: You shot at the SUV, but the villains were not going to let you go that easily. Still your move did have a certain effect on the enemy.
jump.89.text: Shoot at the car from the shotgun
jump.89.desc: Apparently your response scared the guys in the SUV, since the driver started making some sort of signs and reduce the speed. Jeep was falling behind more and more and finally disappeared out of sight altogether.
jump.90.desc:
- Hasta la vista, baby, - you said in a deliberately serious tone, sneered, and started shooting at the SUV. Bang-bang-bang!

The SUV driver went skidding and slowed down. Looks like you made a serious impression on the brave pair, and they thought better of it.
jump.91.text: Try to break away from them
jump.91.desc: You floored the accelerator. The engine roared, and literally started scoffing the gasoline. But to no avail. Looks like the villains are not going top let you go that easily... Maybe you should convince them this was a bad idea on their side?
jump.92.text: Try to break away from them
jump.92.desc: You floored the accelerator and felt you were getting a breakaway. Hurray! Soon the guys in the SUV disappeared out of sight.
jump.93.text: Drop the load on the enemy
jump.93.desc: You moved in front of the SUV, pushed the red button, and dumped your entire load on the enemy. For some time the only thing you could see in your rear-view mirror was a huge cloud of dust. You almost started jumping with joy, when the SUV broke out from the dust. Skidding from one side to another, it finally straightened out and continued the chase. However you still damaged them a bit.
jump.94.text: Drop the load on the enemy
jump.94.desc: You moved in front of the SUV, pushed the red button, and dumped your entire load on the enemy. The load was falling out of the truck like from a cornucopia. The chasers tried to manoeuvre, dodging the falling cargo. But there was too much of it. One of the containers fell right under their wheel, the SUV turned over and rolled into the gutter. So much for the chasers - next time they won't be messing with you!
jump.98.desc: The SUV started slowing down. You were driving further and further away from the villains. Finally they are out of your sight. Looks like the decided to leave you alone.
jump.102.desc:
You went out of the truck and cautiously paid the villains what they asked. 

- That's better, - one of them said, putting the money in his pocket. - You can go now. No one is going to touch you on this road again.
jump.103.text: Fire from a shotgun and split
jump.103.desc: Sticking the shotgun out of the window you fired at the cut-throats and started retreating quickly. But these guys knew what they were doing and started shooting back at you from their crossbows. One of the arrows caught you on the shoulder, but you still managed to escape.
jump.104.text: Try to move back and dash forward down the road
jump.104.desc: You quickly ignited the truck and started steering back onto the road. But the cut-throats were not about to let this happen hat easily - shooting at you from their crossbows. Since they had you in the clear, two titanium arrows went right into your body. However, despite the pain, you still managed to escape. When the punks finally disappeared from sight you stopped and pulled the arrows out...
jump.105.desc:
You went out of the truck and showed them your tat.

- Hey guys, I'm a Scorpion! What's up with that?
- Hmm. I don't seem to remember your face, - one of the cut-throats came over and examined your tattoo. - No. This tattoo is the Bear's handiwork for sure. Well, sorry, bro. Pass.
jump.114.text: Pull over at the gas station
jump.116.text: Ask, where they get gasoline from in this hole
jump.117.text: Ask them to repair your truck
jump.120.text: Ask them to repair your truck
jump.129.desc:
You entered the rut-road and drove to the building. A minute later you were already at the building. The door opened, and a man with a sheriff's star on the chest and two guns on the belt appeared. Two escorts followed him. The guy with the star said:
- I'm the sheriff. Who are you?
- <Ranger>. I come here with peace.
- You must be a new guy... Well, remember this, <Ranger>: if you start any serious trouble in these parts, especially in Shpick, me and my lads here are going to make you regret it.
jump.130.text: I need weapons. You have any?
jump.133.text: Helios-schmelios, who cares! To be honest with you it's all Greek to me, so I'm afraid I can't help you
jump.143.text: The Iroquois have kidnapped Rolan. Please help me find him...
jump.144.text: Some cut-throats are attacking honest folks on the road. I think you - being a sheriff - should be aware of this...
jump.163.text: I wanted to ask a few questions...
jump.166.text: Where can I find the Iroquois?
jump.168.text: What is this meat you are serving?
jump.169.text: I am hungry. Can you make me that 'shroom roast of yours...
jump.169.desc: - There you go, - said the bartender and put an iron sheet in front of you with a roast and some mushrooms. No utensils were provided so you had to eat with your hands. The dish turned out surprisingly good. It was quite filling too.
jump.171.text: I need rest. You have a bed...
jump.171.desc:
- Sure. Hey, kid, show our guest to his room, will you, - the bartender said to a boy in the corner.
The lad led you to the second floor, and opened one of the doors. A couple of people were already sleeping there on separate cots. The boy showed you yours. You paid, fell on the bed and a second later were fast asleep...

When you awoke you felt heaps better. Looking at the clock over the door, you saw that your sleeping time has almost run out. Time to go down.
jump.172.text: I need rest. You have a bed...
jump.172.desc:
- Sure. <clr>5<clrEnd> platinum pieces for the Scorpions as usual... Hey, kid, show our guest to his room, will you, - the bartender said to a boy in the corner.
The lad led you to the second floor, and opened one of the doors. A couple of people were already sleeping there on separate cots. The boy showed you yours. You paid, fell on the bed and a second later were fast asleep...

When you awoke you felt heaps better. Looking at the clock over the door, you saw that your sleeping time has almost run out. Time to go down.
jump.175.text: No I don't want any drinks, thanks
jump.177.text: I want to order a round for everyone!
jump.178.text: No, I think I'll skip on that
jump.180.text: Have a shot of port wine (3 platinum pieces)
jump.181.text: Have a shot of port wine (3 platinum pieces)
jump.185.text: Hit the biker on the head
jump.185.desc: Luckily enough you were in good shape, and punched your opponent right in the face. Good jab!
jump.186.text: Hit the biker on the head
jump.186.desc: You tried to hit your opponent, but by this time your body was not quite under your command anymore. Your hand flew right past his ear, and you fell forward onto him. The biker jumped at the opportunity and had you on the ground, accompanied by the hearty laughter of the spectators. Not wanting to look even funnier you stood up.
jump.187.desc: You punched the biker right in the stomach. Maybe not as efficient as a head-knock, but then again, it's harder to miss that one.
jump.189.desc:
Tired you sank down onto the dusty surface of the planet. 
"Loser", - you heard somebody's voice.

When you came to, you shook the dust off yourself and dragged your feet back to the bar...
jump.190.desc: The Biker knocked you right on the head sending a fan of sparks out of your eyes. The crowd cheered loudly and whistled.
jump.191.desc: The biker punched you a couple of times in the gut. For a moment you couldn't catch your breath back. An evil snarl appeared on the face of your opponent, but his evil joy was premature. You quickly regained your grip.
jump.192.desc: Your opponent didn't do anything waiting for you to make the first move.
jump.195.desc:
- Alright, alright, there's a good lad, - said the biker raising his hands.
 The spectators rushed forward to you and started rocking you up in the air. Suddenly you passed out again...

When you came to you were sitting at the door of the bar. Your right shoulder ached terribly. You looked at it and saw a freshly made tattoo of a Scorpion. Looks like you are in the gang now! Overjoyed you went back inside.
jump.196.text: Hey, guys, come on! No kidding. I don't want to fight anymore!
jump.196.desc:
- Loser, - your opponent shook his head and spat right on your clothes. The rest of the crowd did the same...

Having rubbed the spit off your glorious ranger suit, you took the truck and returned back on the road.
jump.197.desc:
The bartender put a case of port wine bottle on the bar.

- Say! The brave driver is buying! - one of the tatted guys yelled.

The rest of it was a blur. You drank port wine together with the bikers, said some obscene toasts, laughed. You also remember a garbage can, darkness, and then you are sitting in the middle of the field with this punk.

- <Ranger>? You wanna join the gang? - he said in a drunken voice.
- Hick! Sure! - you said.
- Hey, boys!! The chief here wants to join the gang, - the punk yelled and a crowd of Scorpions surrounded you.

- Alright, <Ranger>. In order to join the gang you have to fight me and win, - said the punk you just been drinking with. - Stand up and get ready!
jump.198.desc:
The bartender put a case of port wine bottle on the bar. 
- Say! The brave driver is buying! - one of the tatted guys yelled.

The rest of it was a blur. You drank port wine together with the bikers, said some obscene toasts, laughed. Then you tried to crack a joke and suddenly puked all over the bar.

- Shit! Get this nitwit out of here! - the bartender exclaimed and two big blokes threw you out into the street.

When you came to, first thing you did was clean your own clothes from the contents of your stomach, climbed back into your truck and drove to the road. Right. When you plan to do some excessive drinking, you need to be in good healthy shape Not tired as hell...
jump.201.desc:
- We are not drinking port wine, ordered by losers! - the Scorpions standing at the bar said.
- But I do! - said a toothless geezer, who appeared from out of nowhere, put all the bottles into his sack, and disappeared again.

Damn! What a waste...
jump.202.desc:
- Our newbie, <Ranger>, is throwing a party! - one of Scorpions yelled, his voice joined by loud cheering, and then it was a total mayhem. You know as it always happens: port wine, laughter, port wine, roar, port wine, brawl, port wine, "catch-a-dipus-on-a-SUV", port wine, snap...

When you came to you were lying in the corner of the barroom, luckily enough none of your bones were broken. You head was aching, but that would be over soon...
jump.203.desc:
- Hello! - you said friendly.
- Get lost, scum! - a huge guy with a Scorpion tattoo on his forehead barked.

Right... These boys are not that easygoing.
jump.206.text: Let's go have some fun. Scare them geezers. Pad'em all!!!
jump.208.text: Do you have any serious weapons? I'd buy some from you...
jump.210.desc: For the next ten minutes you and the bikers were talking engines, crossbows, and drinking. Nothing interesting. Finally you had enough of it and decided to take your leave.
jump.213.text: Sorry I am a bit busy now
jump.217.text: Where do you get gasoline from?
jump.219.text: I need to repair my flivver. Can you help?
jump.227.text: If this is Stilt's Gas Station, where's Stoltz?
jump.232.text: I need to get my truck fixed...
jump.233.text: No I can't afford it, I'm afraid...
jump.236.text: I see you are truly an enthusiast of your own trade. Can you upgrade my truck somehow?
jump.237.text: I see. Let's discuss some other issues
jump.238.text: I have 5 tons of scrap metal on me right now. Take it and get down to business
jump.239.text: Deal. I'm paying and you increase my truck's carrying capacity
jump.240.text: Are you selling anything? Or maybe you're interested in buying something?
jump.241.text: The Iroquois have kidnapped this guy called Rolan. Can you help me save him?
jump.252.text: Ask what the plant is producing
jump.254.text: Enter the building with a flag
jump.254.desc:
You opened a massive wooden door and went inside of the white house. To the left of the door there stood a solid table. A girl was sitting at the table and typing something furiously on a typewriter. Not looking up at you she said:
- The Mayor is not here for another two or three weeks. So please, clear the premises. 

Well, she does not leave you much choice on that one, does she?
jump.255.text: Walk about the town looking for other places of interest
jump.255.desc: You walked about the town for some time but found nothing aside from shabby old residential buildings. Looks like all the necessary stuff is located in the main square. Having arrived to this conclusion, you went back to where you started.
jump.256.text: Walk about the town looking for other places of interest
jump.256.desc: You walked about the town for some time but found nothing aside from shabby old residential buildings. Looks like all the necessary stuff is located in the main square. Having arrived to this conclusion, you turned back. You put your hand in your pocket and discovered that someone has stolen a couple of platinum pieces from you... This discovery did not really improve your mood.
jump.257.text: Walk about the town looking for other places of interest
jump.257.desc:
You walked about the town for some time but found nothing aside from shabby old residential buildings. Looks like all the necessary stuff is located in the main square. Having arrived to this conclusion, you turned back when somebody hit you on the head from behind. The blow was so strong and unexpected that you fell down.

 - Death to the immigrants! - you heard somebody shout. Rolling over on your back you saw three youngsters of typically delinquent appearance loom over you. You would easily step up against each of them separately, but once they were together they were becoming a strong force.

Judging buy the look of them they were not very friendly. Then again you weren't either. Rising back to your feet, you kicked one of the assailants between the legs, then broke the other one's nose with a right hook. After which the drunken company quickly retreated. But they hit you good too. You really shouldn't be wandering about the town alone at this time. Dusk is the best friend of all delinquents.
jump.258.text: What is the climate here like?
jump.260.text: Walk about the town looking for other places of interest
jump.262.text: Throw a couple of platinum pieces to the old man
jump.262.desc:
- Thanks, son, - the beggar said. - I see you are a traveller. Let me give you this advice. If you go down the road from here to Mow's Gas Station you will see a turn which leads to a lake. Looks like your regular dirty lake. But <clr>if you swim in this lake for some 15 minutes and all your wounds will skin over <clrEnd> miraculously. Go in peace, now.

Remembering the old man's advice, you walked back tom the square.
jump.266.desc:
You took the door handle and noticed a plate that read:
"<clr>Open<clrEnd>.
Restaurant open daily:
from 9:00 and to the last client after 23:59"

Taking a mental note of the fact you entered. The place was not exactly packed and you quickly found yourself a table.
jump.270.text: Chef's special: cactuses in kinza sauce - 23 platinum pieces
jump.273.text: Thanks for your hospitality. I think I'll go now
jump.276.text: Wait for the restaurant to open
jump.276.desc: You stood there waiting for the restaurant to open. Finally it happened! At about 9:00 the restaurant opened, you went inside and sat at one of the tables. Looks like you are the first visitor here tonight!
jump.278.text: Thank you I don't want anything
jump.280.desc: The room turned out to be quite cosy. And there wasn't anyone else there, so you really had yourself a good rest. Some time later you went back into the square.
jump.281.text: Girls sound like a good idea. So yes, please, full service
jump.281.desc:
The woman at the reception desk found you a proper girl and sent her to your room.

Everything went great. Even the plaster fell off the ceiling in several spots. That was truly a good rest! When you woke up your female companion was gone. Too bad. You could give it another go. Having combed your hair and dressed you went back into the square.
jump.282.desc:
- Thanks, bro. Don't be afraid. Once I'm in the cabin I'll fall asleep straight away and you won't even notice me.

You led the Peleng to the truck and locked him in the cabin. And indeed - he was out the same instance, just like that! Still you screwed out the sparking plug - just in case. With this done you went back to the bar.
jump.283.text: Who is this guy sleeping on the table in the corner?
jump.285.desc:
Stopping in the middle of the square you tried to wake the Peleng up. As if it was that easy! You had to shake him for a good five minutes, until he finally opened his eyes.
- What? What is it? - the Peleng was startled still half-asleep. 
- We're here!
- Indeed! Hey, thanks, bro! You know I am done with the wild life anyway, I came here to work at the plant. So here, take this trophy shotgun and six cartridges to it. I am sure you will put it to good use, - from out of nowhere the Peleng produced a small shotgun with six cartridges and gave it to you. - Well, so long.
With these words the Peleng took off in the direction of the plant and soon disappeared out of sight.
jump.299.text: Take a quick dive in the lake and go back
jump.299.desc: A short water constitutional refreshed you a bit. Now you could go back to the road.
jump.301.text: Get out of the water, dry up and return back to the road.
jump.302.desc:
You continued swimming. Suddenly you felt <clr>your body fill with energy<clrEnd>, and your wounds skin over. Looks like this lake has some healing effect to it!
A couple of minutes later the positive effect of the lake stopped. Apparently in your current condition of "healthiness" the lake cannot produce any more positive effect on you. Once you understood this, you climbed out onto the shore, dried yourself, got into your truck and drove back the freeway.
jump.303.desc: You continued swimming. Mosquitoes buzzing over your head, gleet filling your mouth. For crying out loud! Finally you got completely sick and tired of this, climbed out onto the shore, dried yourself, got into your truck and drove back the freeway.
jump.310.text: Try to break away from them
jump.310.desc: You floored the accelerator and felt that you were making breakaway. Hurray! Soon the armoured car disappeared out of sight altogether.
jump.311.text: Drop the load on the enemy
jump.311.desc: You moved in front of the opponent, pushed the red button, and dumped your entire load on the enemy. The load was falling out of the truck like from a cornucopia. Taking a look back you spotted the enemy who was struggling desperately to drive out of the pile, formed by the dumped load. By the time they make it, you will be a long, long way from here.
jump.312.desc:
You went out of the truck and cautiously paid the villains what they asked. 

- That's better, - one of them said, putting the money in his pocket. - You can go now. No one is going to touch you on this road again.
jump.313.desc: You took your shotgun and fired at the cut-throats. Scared of what they thought could follow, they went running. And you climbed back into the truck and continued about your own business.
jump.314.text: Rush back to the truck and run away
jump.314.desc: You rushed back to your truck but one of the cut-throats jumped upon you. You fell on the ground struggling... The other villain did not interfere and watched, sure of his comrade. But, as luck would have it, you still had some strength left and you managed to put up some serious resistance - the enemy fell and rolled into the gutter. The second bandit tried to catch you, but you were already in your truck and floored the accelerator. When you were already a good distance away from them, you felt a shot of pain. This cut-throat has seriously injured you after all.
jump.317.text: Hit the other car with your truck
jump.317.desc: You jolted the steering wheel sending the truck sideways onto the enemy, but their car was well-armoured and your attack attempt did not cause much damage.
jump.318.text: Hit the other car with your truck
jump.318.desc: Despite their car being well-armoured you still managed to inflict a lot of damage on it with your spikes.
jump.319.text: Shoot at the car from the shotgun
jump.319.desc: And shoot you did. But what's the point? They are armoured. Your small shots are nothing to it.
jump.320.text: Try to break away from them
jump.320.desc: You floored the accelerator but still couldn't make a breakaway. Looks like your chasers are not going to give it up that easily. Maybe you should try to cool off their enthusiasm?
jump.321.text: Drop the load on the enemy
jump.321.desc: You moved in front of the opponent, pushed the red button, and dumped your entire load on the enemy. But this was pretty useless - your load was too small to stop the enemy.
jump.326.desc: The armoured passenger vehicle started reducing its speed. The distance between you and the gangsters was increasing more and more. Finally you lost sight of them. Looks like they decided to leave you alone.
jump.327.desc: You shot at the enemy's car three times, but what good it was. They got armour.
jump.328.desc:
- That's right, you weak pathetic Scorpion! - the cut-throat threw you on the ground, climbed back into his car, and they took off. 

Phew, that was close. You went back to your truck and continued on your business. Next time better not flash you Scorpion tattoo in front of these hoodlums...
jump.330.text: You bastards!!! Alright, come on, come on! Kill me! And let the Scorpions avenge my death!!!
jump.331.desc: Incredible!!! You managed to catch him under celiac plexus. The Iroquois who was holding you bent in half. The second one was too surprised to do anything. Using his bewilderment, you quickly ran to your truck and took off. Now it was too late for them to chase you!
jump.332.text: Rush back to the truck and run away
jump.333.desc: You took out your shotgun and fired at the cut-throats. One of them took to his heels, but the other one seemed to be of a braver lot. However, one blow with the butt of the shotgun on the head calmed him down as well. Although, the scumbag did manage to cut you a couple of times too.
jump.334.desc:
You aimed the shotgun - bang! Bang! Bang!... One of the cut-throats went a-running into the field, while the second one remained lying wounded on the asphalt. Well, be smarter next time. 
Climbing back into your truck you went off.
jump.342.text: Try to break away from them
jump.342.desc: You floored the accelerator but could not shake the chase off. Your <clr>truck is overloaded<clrEnd>, which is why you cannot make it.
jump.343.text: Try to break away from them
jump.343.desc: You floored the accelerator. The engine roared scoffing the gasoline, but to no avail. Looks like, <clr>you are too overloaded<clrEnd>, to break away from the chase...
jump.353.text: Repair the truck, using the parts of your old truck
jump.353.desc:
You spent a lot of time with the truck mending it here and there. Finally you started all of the fuel form the old truck into your new steel buffalo. You started up the engine - but no. You had to fumble with it a little more. And again, and more again. 

Until finally - a miracle! The engine started. You moved a bit forward, stopped, and started carrying everything from the cabin of the old truck, into the new one. Then you somehow reloaded all of your cargo into the bodywork of the new truck and were about to take off. When your old truck suddenly rolled back and fell down the canyon. No wonder you did remove the brakes too. Too bad. Then again this old machine was no good anymore anyway...

You climbed into your new steel friend, and drove back to the farm. It seemed that the new truck was a lot slower than the old one, but its capacity was larger too.
jump.359.text: Fill the truck with spinach to the brim
jump.363.text: Have you got any weapons? I think I could buy some
jump.364.text: I need money. Could I work a little on your farm?
jump.377.text: I want to pay the ransom for Rolan!
jump.378.text: I want to pay the ransom for Rolan!
jump.381.text: Drive into the territory of the airport
jump.387.text: Alright, it's pretty clear. Time to mount the truck and go save Rolan
jump.388.text: Go to Ramina's house and ask her a couple of questions
jump.389.desc: Cleaning yourself some space from all kinds of junk, you made yourself a bed in the backseat. And although your sleep wasn't that long - folks coming back forth awoke you - and although it was not that comfortable, it was still free!
jump.400.text: Refuse to exchange and go back to your ship
jump.402.desc:
Cleaning yourself some space from all kinds of junk, you made yourself a bed in the backseat. When suddenly the spell of your dream was broke with some strange sounds. You woke up and saw <clr>several teenagers hitting your truck with sticks <clrEnd>. Outraged you jumped outside but the youth was gone already.

"You buy them books, you send them to school and what do you end up with - the little bastards!" - you thought to yourself, climbing back into the truck.
jump.404.text: What's up with that company at the bar?
jump.406.text: Head back to the slot machine
jump.407.text: Go away from the slot machine
jump.413.text: Go away from the slot machine
jump.414.desc: You dropped a platinum piece into the slot, pulled the lever, and... broke it off. Damn! <clr>You broke the slot machine.<clrEnd> But apparently so far no one noticed. Now you have to quickly and quietly disappear...
jump.415.text: Fire three shot from the shotgun and split
jump.415.desc: You fired three shot from the shotgun. One of the villains took to his heels immediately. The second one hid behind the SUV. And you drove out onto the freeway and split.
jump.422.desc:
You were about to go off when a grimy miner ran u to your truck:
- Hey, chief! Can you give me a lift to <clr>Shpick<clrEnd>? I'll pay you <clr>40 platinum pieces<clrEnd>?
jump.424.text: I got different plans right now, sorry
jump.425.desc:
You started the engine and drove to the exit, when you noticed a guy waving his hand by the road and stopped. A strong-knit miner walked up to your truck:
- Hey, chief! I am going to drink away my pay. Can you give me a lift to the <clr>Scorpion nest<clrEnd>? I am paying <clr>60<clrEnd>.
jump.427.desc:
- Shit! Where the hell are we! - your travelling companion was outraged. - I should have found me a proper driver in the first place.

You tried to explain to him that you only dropped by here, since it was in the same direction. But the passenger wouldn't listen. Oh well. There goes your money...
jump.428.desc: - Thanks, bro! The miner gave you <clr>60 platinum pieces<clrEnd> and trotted off to the bar.
jump.430.desc:
- Damn! John Long the carrier! - your travelling companion was outraged. - I should have found me a proper driver in the first place.

You tried to explain it to him, that you were just about to go, but to no avail. The passenger wouldn't listen. Oh well. There goes your money...
jump.431.desc: - Home at last! - your travelling companion exclaimed, gave you the promised <clr>40<clrEnd> platinum pieces and disappeared down one of the streets.
jump.432.desc:
Stopping in the middle of the square you tried to wake the Peleng up. As if it was that easy! You had to shake him for a good five minutes, until he finally opened his eyes.
- What? What is it? - the Peleng was startled still half-asleep. 
- We're here!
- Indeed! Hey, thanks, bro! You know I am done with the wild life anyway, I came here to work at the plant. So here, take this trophy shotgun and six cartridges to it. I am sure you will put it to good use, - from out of nowhere the Peleng produced a small shotgun with six cartridges and gave it to you. - Well, so long.
With these words the Peleng took off in the direction of the plant and soon disappeared out of sight.
jump.434.text: Drive into the territory of the airport
jump.434.desc:
- Shit! Where the hell are we! - your travelling companion was outraged. - I should have found me a proper driver in the first place.

You tried to explain to him that you only dropped by here, since it was in the same direction. But the passenger wouldn't listen. Oh well. There goes your money...
jump.435.desc:
- Shit! Where the hell are we! - your travelling companion was outraged. - I should have found me a proper driver in the first place.

You tried to explain to him that you only dropped by here, since it was in the same direction. But the passenger wouldn't listen. Oh well. There goes your money...
jump.436.desc:
A slightly drunken lad clad in a miner's hard hat ran up to your truck:
- Hick... Chief can you give me a lift to the <clr>mines<clrEnd>? - he blurted out grabbing the handle in a feeble attempt to keep his balance. - I'm paying <clr>38 platinum pieces<clrEnd>. That's all I got left...
jump.438.text: I got different plans right now, sorry
jump.439.desc:
The moment you started up the engine some completely drunken guy climbed into the cabin and said:
- Let's get moving, chief. The next stop is <clr>Shpick<clrEnd>. I'm paying <clr>100 platinum pieces<clrEnd>, fact!
jump.441.desc:
- Shit! Where the hell are we! - your travelling companion was outraged. - I should have found me a proper driver in the first place.

You tried to explain to him that you only dropped by here, since it was in the same direction. But the passenger wouldn't listen. Oh well. There goes your money...
jump.442.desc: - Thanks, chap! I owe you bigtime - said your travel companion, gave you all of his coins (it was exactly <clr>38 platinum pieces<clrEnd>) and walked off to the barracks.
jump.443.desc: - Watch it go! Let the madness continue. Now let us spend some money here in Shpick. Hey, chief, here's your <clr>100<clrEnd> platinum pieces, - you travelling companion gave you the money, slammed the door behind him, and staggered off from the car.

You truck was slowly rolling out onto the freeway, when you heard somebody knock on the window. It was one of the sheriff's assistants:
- I need to go to <clr>Shpick<clrEnd> on a business trip. Can you give me a lift? - the law enforcement officer asked. I can only pay in kind, I mean: if you give me a lift <clr>I will give you 8 shotgun rounds <clrEnd>. Deal?
jump.450.text: I got different plans right now, sorry
jump.451.desc: You truck was slowly rolling out onto the freeway, when you heard somebody knock on the window. It was one of the sheriff's assistants: - I got to go to the Digsons' farm. Need to agree on some supplies for the lads, you know. Can you give me a lift? And In will pay you <clr>50 platinum pieces<clrEnd> out of the company money.
jump.452.desc:
- On behalf of Law Enforcement Department No3 I express my gratitude, driver! - the guy in uniform barked and jumped out into the street.
- Hey, are you gonna pay or what? - you shouted to him.
- Oh yes, - the guy walked back to the truck and gave you <clr>8<clrEnd> cartridges. - Leaving the sheriff's officers without ammo... Who's going to protect you when the going gets tough?
- Don't worry, tough I can handle, - you answered taking the rounds from him.

jump.455.desc:
You stopped right at the farmer's house to drop off your travelling companion.

- Excellent. Just where I wanted it. Now our the lads back art the department will not die of hunger, - he said, gave you 50 platinum pieces, and headed for the farmhouse.
jump.456.desc:
You were just about to go off, when a man in business suit ran over to the truck:
- Excuse me. I need to see the <clr>sheriff<clrEnd>, to settle certain red tape matters. Can you give me a lift? I can pay! I can pay <clr>50<clrEnd> platinum pieces.
jump.458.text: I got different plans right now, sorry
jump.459.desc:
You were just about to go off, when this lad ran over up to your truck:
- Chief! Are you heading for the <clr>mines<clrEnd> by any chance? I hear one could earn a whole pile of platinum there - and that's something I just can't miss! What do you say? I will pay you well too - <clr>30<clrEnd> platinum pieces!
jump.460.desc:
- Thanks for the lift, - the man said brushing the dust off his suit. Here's your <clr>50<clrEnd> platinum pieces. Oh yes, should you have any problems with tap water in any apartment in Shpick, here's my number - I am the water supply deputy E.C. Yellowtailer.

The travelling companion gave you his business card and took off.
jump.461.desc: - Here we go, baby! Soon I will become rich, - the boy cried out, jumping out of the car. - Hey, chap, here're are your <clr>30 platinum pieces<clrEnd>. And! Don't forget to drink a glass of wine or two to my success.
jump.482.text: Fire from a shotgun and split
jump.482.desc: You fired at the cut-throats from the shotgun and started retreating. The villains however were not of most cowardice type and began shooting back from their crossbows. Fortunately enough they never hit you, and you quickly drove off.
jump.483.text: Drive into the territory of the airport
jump.485.text: I'd gladly pay you but I don't have the money. Maybe we can resolve this issue amicably... I mean - diplomatically. No?
jump.486.desc:
One of the villains walked over to your truck, swung the door open and pulled you out on the ground. He searched your pockets and called out to his comrade:
- This guy has got [p6] on him.
- The titanium-searcher says there's nothing in the truck either, - the second responded. - Looks like he's telling the truth. He is broke. Well. So what do we do with him?
- Look in the truck, maybe we could use some of his cargo - anything that looks valuable - load it in our SUV.
This phrase was the last thing you remembered before a shot of pain knocked you unconscious. Looks like they knocked you out.

When you came to you were lying on the road. No truck, no money, nothing... Having taken a look in the bodywork you saw that a large part of your load was gone. How come? You climbed into the cabin and continued on your way.
jump.489.text: Wait, but I don't have that money! Maybe we can resolve this issue in some other way?
jump.490.desc: When you came to you were lying in the gutter. Your sides were aching badly but at least you could move. You staggered back to the truck, climbed in your seat, and drove off. Phew. These Iroquois are real madmen. Next time you really should avoid such meetings. Unless you have a big shotgun.
jump.491.text: Direct your steps to the medical station
jump.492.text: I really do not feel well. I could use some energy treatment...
jump.493.text: What other procedure can you offer?
jump.505.desc: Completing the deal, you put the cartridge into your pocket, all proud of yourself.
jump.508.text: Sorry, comrade. I 'm afraid I can't afford it. Haven't got enough gas for myself.
jump.509.desc: You took the money, pumped off some gas from you truck and fuelled the trucker.
jump.510.text: You are pulling my leg, right! I am not going to sell fuel for as little as {[p33]}
jump.512.text: You are pulling my leg, right! I am not going to sell fuel for as little as {[p33]}
jump.512.desc: Not wanting to bargain the driver stomped the accelerator, leaving a cloud of exhaust smoke behind him. One should not be too greedy - fact. With these thought you continued about your business.
jump.513.desc: - What am I carrying? Nothing really. I'm empty, - the driver responded.
jump.517.text: Alright. Get that spinach over here
jump.518.text: Two tons of scrap metal? Sure!
jump.519.text: I'm good with just one ton
jump.520.text: Say, friend. Could you sell me about 15 litres of gas? I'm running out.
jump.520.desc: - Sorry, I barely got enough myself to make it. Sorry.

jump.541.desc: - Hmm... No. I don't need it.
jump.550.text: Not interested, understand. End of story!
jump.550.desc: - Well, up to you. This was a good proposal, - with these words the fuel truck took off, and you continued about your business.
jump.551.text: Sure get that gas here now!
jump.551.desc: Quickly pouring the oily liquid into your gas tank, the fuel truck driver took the money and waved you good bye. You started up the engine and went off too. Looks like this gasoline is of decent quality, since the engine did not cough up and die. At least for now...
jump.555.text: Hmmmm.... I think I'll take the Snatcher legs
jump.557.text: Well, whatever, let me try the stew
jump.560.text: Say goodbye to the healer and go off
jump.564.text: Hey, chief, I got some spinach back there. Wanna buy?
jump.564.desc: - Nah, thanks. Got a truckload of it myself! - the trucker replied.
jump.565.text: Say, partner, I got me some scrap metal back there. Wanna buy?
jump.565.desc: - No way! I got a full truckload of this stuff myself.
jump.566.desc: - Some coal, some scrap metal, - the trucker replied.
jump.567.desc: - Wine, port wine, kinza, - the driver responded. - And wipe that grin off your face now, I am not selling you anything. It's a purchase order, so go figure.
jump.568.desc:
- Err, I don't like these questions, - the trucker mumbled. 
- Well, don't answer then.
jump.572.desc: Your mighty hit threw the assailant's car to the side, one of his wheels broke off, the vehicle skidded and hurled over three times. After which the iron tin of these loser flew off to the gutter losing semi-rusted parts. Got it! Next time they will think twice before harassing honest truckers.
jump.574.desc: Your mighty hit threw the assailant's car to the side. The unsteady SUV ran on two wheels for some time, and for a second it even looked that they just might make it, but then all the other damage kicked in, suddenly the front axis broke off and jerked to the side. The driver desperately tried to save the day, but it was useless. The vehicle started to zigzag, tumbled over and rolled into the gutter, where it stayed in a cloud of smoke. Great! Another butcher down the gutter.

jump.581.desc:
Leaving your truck at the penalty lot you went off to talk to the sheriff. The sheriff spent a long time reviewing the reports of his subordinates, heard your story out, and finally decided you were not guilty of breaking the traffic rules. The entire investigation took <clr>about an hour<clrEnd>. 
But your joy was premature - when you came back to the penalty lot you found that a whole <clr>ton of scrap metal<clrEnd> was missing from the truck! Well, you cannot blame these guys, they have to make road signs out of something... 
Still your mood was spoiled.
jump.582.desc: Leaving your truck at the penalty lot you went off to talk to the sheriff. Unfortunately the sheriff was too busy and could only receive you <clr>in two hours<clrEnd>. It took him another hour to review the reports of his subordinates, and hear out your story. Finally with obvious unwillingness he was forced to pronounce you not guilty of breaking the traffic rules. When you left the penalty lot you were tired, but were in a good mood - you managed to prove your righteousness!!!
jump.583.desc:
Leaving your truck at the penalty lot you went off to talk to the sheriff. The sheriff decided to be serious about it: he studied the detailed reports of his subordinates, listened to your side of the story and asked you a whole lot of all kinds of questions. Finally, <clr>some two hours later<clrEnd> the sheriff's fantasy was exhausted, and he wrote you a pass from the penalty lot. 
But when you went back to your truck you found that <clr>some of the parts were missing<clrEnd>! The guard at the lot played a fool and kept repeating that he saw nothing. You could not prove anything and were forced to leave the lot as is...
